correctness.rationale: Fully specified Hilbert cross-ratio normalization and Dirichlet gamma construction reduce the problem to an independent beta-prime logarithmic range. Standalone package checker passed direct simplex pair sampling and independent quadrature comparisons; finite numeric tests do not replace proofs.

originality.rationale: The highly relevant 2023 numerical histograms of Hilbert distances between independent uniform simplex points do not state an analytic pair-distance law. The 2004 metric classification and 2017 clustering paper provide geometry but no Dirichlet range CDF or jointly independent extrema. The own fixed-center result gives an implicit two-point law after averaging only at alpha=1; it does not imply the all-alpha Dirichlet family, alpha-dependent sharp small balls, joint Gumbel-sum scaling or variance. No equivalent published-finding corpus or primary-source theorem was located in actual queries; absence of a search hit is not treated as proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: Symmetric Dirichlet measures are natural probability-simplex sampling models, and the same Hilbert distance is used in applied geometry/embedding literature with numerical pair-distance histograms. The general-alpha exact CDF, sharp radius coefficient and concentration-dependent two-Gumbel calibration give interpretable all-dimensional metric invariants and reproduce the exact Euclidean-volume harmonic mean. These quantify the phenomenon beyond routine resubstitution or a small numeric improvement; nothing is claimed for other domains or measures.
